scope: Strict checking of existing numerical-frame and live-channel writer bodies, with shared prepared-result and borrowed callback contracts.

validation.installed_package_smoke: passed: installed types, SSR, production rendering at DPR 2, settings, fonts, remounts, coordinate frames and JAX inputs

contracts: Live-channel getters borrow target/display preparations from the shared PreparedMark record.
afterWrites borrows temporary values until its promise resolves; consumers retain any published arrays. finally preserves the existing releases.
Serialized queues preserve callback result types, skip newer-order superseded work and permit a later batch after rejection.
Numerical frame mapping borrows option/stage owners, copies and freezes validated intervals, and names forward/inverse numerical scales without camera state.
Lazy view-state input functions are named alongside ViewStateRecord; the viewState body itself is not newly strict-checked.
limitations: Executable source identity after type/comment erasure is not a new performance measurement or a claim of identical flight/readback counts.
No actual Svelte module is newly strict-checked; its request/action/result producers and consumers remain pending.
Numerical mapping does not complete the root-promotion Svelte handoff or checking of all JAX/WGSL consumers.
Dynamic evaluator payloads remain validated by array conversion and field writers; annotations introduce no runtime defaults or new validation paths.
No new public props, generated API inputs, runtime node capabilities, scheduler or wrapper module.
